newsitem.title: USA: Donnelley to shed software services - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Donnelley to shed software services - WSJ.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co intends to sell part or all of Stream International, a software services company, The Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
The story says the move would free the largest U.S. commercial printer from a cash drain.
"One big mistake this company made was Stream," Edward Atorino, an analyst at Oppenheimer & Co is quoted as saying.
Though an initial round of discussions this year failed to find an adequate suitor for Stream, the parent company is now exploring ways to sell the company piece by piece, the story says.
Donnelley, which owns 80 percent of Stream, believes the business is worth between $700 million and $1.2 billion, the story says.
